title: Los Altos
capsule: Los Altos was a liberal state proclaimed on 2 February 1838 when delegates at Quetzaltenango declared independence from Guatemala, constituting themselves the sixth state of the dissolving Federal Republic of Central America, with their capital at Quetzaltenango in the western Guatemalan highlands. The state drew support from mestizo and indigenous communities seeking autonomy from Guatemala City's conservative creole establishment and from liberal Guatemalan exiles. Conservative caudillo Rafael Carrera invaded and suppressed it in January 1840; a brief revival in August 1848 lasted only until Carrera retook Quetzaltenango on 8 May 1849, definitively ending Los Altos as a political entity.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The claimed territory of Los Altos — eight western Guatemalan departments — is stated in the independence proclamation; the state never exercised stable control across this area, and the dataset records it from 1838 to 1842, capturing its first and most substantive phase.
